items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Some of the jokes were: How do you feel, Mr. Bones? and Mr. Bones would answer: Just like a stove!

ctx.x: Dolly Jones left Cincinnati along with her mother who's name was Dyer Jones. Some medicine shows came to town and they used to put on their show in any empty lot they could find and no one had to pay to see them. The supposed doctor sold bottles of syrup that was supposed to be good for the liver, rheumatism, heart trouble, and pills for blood circulation, aching bones or any kind of sickness that existed. Medicine to cure all ailments.

There were always some kind of musicians playing those shows and a couple of comedians. Some of the jokes were: How do you feel, Mr. Bones? and Mr. Bones would answer: Just like a stove! The other one would ask: How's that? and Mr. Bones would answer: Red hot and still a heating.

Another one was: How do you feel to-night, Mr. Sampson? Mr. Sampson would say: Just like that woman's mouth, and point to some woman in the crowd. The other one who was usually known as the straight man would ask: How's that? and Sampson would say: wide open.
